acceptance: Per PR and per merge, for a stated UTC window with complete collection (no 1,000-result truncation), the report lists every workflow that ran for the same head, with run counts, attempts, conclusions, cancellations, summed job runner-minutes and job queue time median and p90, for oracle-review, oracle-verdict, oracle-gate, ci-text-edit-refresh, pr-hold, ci.yml and the path-dependent siblings
The report separates cancelled work from completed work and identifies redundant same-head or same-event runs, with counts and runner-minutes

The report shows, per workflow, whether it lies on the critical path to all required checks ready (core, docs, explorer, results-data, tooling, hold, oracle-gate), using the time-to-green measure from the CI usage report

A ranked recommendation compares oracle and text-edit fan-out reduction with medium shard balancing and further test trimming by measured runner-minutes and time-to-green effect, and states what each reduction would preserve (current-head binding, invalidation, required status delivery) or give up
Owner decision recorded: which candidate reductions, if any, are approved for implementation; each approved one gets its own item
The result and the window and sample counts it rests on are recorded on this item
context:
OWNER DECISION 2026-10-25: no oracle-related changes from this effort; the verdict-to-gate latency lever is logged as oracle-gate-verdict-to-status-latency-20261025 for an agent that owns oracle work. No other reductions approved; runner capacity stays deferred. Closing the study.

RESULT 2026-10-25 (window 2026-10-24T00:00Z to 2026-10-25T15:02Z: 5,133 runs, 13,098 jobs, 83 merged PRs, 229 PR heads, 90 all-green heads; 7 job-page retrievals failed, none for oracle or text-edit runs). Oracle family plus pr-hold plus ci-text-edit-refresh used 1,542 of 26,685 runner-minutes (5.8%, about 19 of 320 minutes per merge); ci.yml 65.7%, Trunk workflows 23.9%. Pool peaked at 20 concurrent jobs; while a CI job queued over 300 s, about 14 CI and 0.7 oracle-family jobs were running, so CI queueing is self-inflicted. oracle-gate was the last required context on 58 of 90 green heads, landing a median 1,235 s after the last CI context, mostly waiting for the SHIP verdict; the verdict-to-gate bridge is median 54 s, p90 779 s (queue). Cancelled work 1,007 min (3.8%), about 97 oracle-family; oracle-gate's ~877 cancellations mostly never start a runner. ci-text-edit-refresh 902 runs, 75.9 min. Ranked: (1) CI queue relief inside ci.yml; (2) test trimming in medium, fast and correctness-gate groups (~13,000 of 17,500 CI minutes); (3) medium shard balance (~40 s time-to-green where core is last); (4) oracle-gate bridge tail (up to ~780 s p90 on gate-bound heads, soundness path, needs maintainer review); (5) oracle-verdict duplicate runs (<=350 min, risk to verdict freshness); (6) trigger fan-out cuts not recommended; (7) text-edit refresh and path siblings: no action. Acceptance 1-4 met; 5 (owner decision on approved reductions) open.

description: Several workflows run for the same pull-request head, not only CI. Unconditional develop-PR siblings: ci.yml, pr-hold.yml, oracle-review.yml, oracle-verdict.yml, oracle-gate.yml. Path-dependent siblings: extension-smoke.yml, gitignore-lint.yml, tpcds-platform-identity.yml, tpch-dbgen-intel-macos.yml. Completion-driven work: ci-text-edit-refresh.yml (runs after CI completes) and further oracle-gate runs after oracle workflow completion. Post-merge sibling: site-inputs.yml, triggered by Trunk completion. test.yml, lint.yml, perf-smoke.yml and validate-release-pr.yml target the release branch, not ordinary develop PRs. In a capped all-workflow sample of 1,000 runs spanning about 14 hours on 2026-10-24 (not a full day, and not a daily rate), oracle-gate had 414 runs (193 cancelled), oracle-review 130, oracle-verdict 105, ci-text-edit-refresh 147, CI 64 and Trunk 17; the first four are 796 of 1,000 workflow invocations. Invocations are not occupied runner jobs, and no oracle job data exists yet to say how much runner time is wasted. Using the output of ci-usage-metrics-report-20261024, measure real job occupancy, cancellations, redundant same-head or same-event work, and each workflow's contribution to the final all-required-checks-ready time, then rank oracle and text-edit fan-out against shard balancing and further test trimming. Do not remove oracle checks or combine trust domains here: oracle-review and the App-bound oracle-gate have different enforcement roles, and any reduction must preserve current-head binding, invalidation and required status delivery. oracle-gate is the required oracle check on develop since PR #3395; oracle-review is no longer required. Also account for the prospective load and workflow-completion latency of canary-impact-04-shadow-job, which stays a separate item. This is an investigation; its output is a ranked recommendation and, if warranted, new items.
